guide.instructions: Handwriting simplified Chinese characters. The learner is a heritage Mandarin speaker who is learning to read through the `chinese` pack (HSK order) and wants to write the most common characters by hand. Each card is ONE character. Front (Prompt): a familiar word with the target character replaced by ＿, then the whole word's pinyin, then its meaning, e.g. '＿习 · xuéxí · to study'. It must point to exactly one character and must not contain the answer. The learner writes the character on paper, then flips. Hanzi: the single character. Pinyin: its reading in that word. Notes: components with meanings (学 = ⺍ + 冖 cover + 子 child), the exact stroke count, the order the parts are written in, any stroke-order trap, and lookalikes. Lessons have 15 characters, follow the order characters first appear in the HSK reading lessons, and each lesson body points out recurring components and one or two stroke-order rules.
